{{short description|Theorem about commutative rings and subrings}}
In algebra, the '''theorem of transition''' is said to hold between [[commutative ring]]s <math>A \subset B</math> if<ref>{{harvnb|Nagata|1975|loc=Ch. II, § 19.}}</ref><ref name=Matsumura>{{harvnb|Matsumura|1986|loc=Ch. 8, Exercise 22.1.}}</ref>
# <math>B</math> dominates <math>A</math>; i.e., for each proper ideal ''I'' of ''A'', <math>IB</math> is proper and for each maximal ideal <math>\mathfrak n</math> of ''B'', <math>\mathfrak n \cap A</math> is maximal
# for each maximal ideal <math>\mathfrak m</math> and <math>\mathfrak m</math>-primary ideal <math>Q</math> of <math>A</math>, <math>\operatorname{length}_B (B/ Q B)</math> is finite and moreover
#:<math>\operatorname{length}_B (B/ Q B) = \operatorname{length}_B (B/ \mathfrak{m} B) \operatorname{length}_A(A/Q).</math>

Given commutative rings <math>A \subset B</math> such that <math>B</math> dominates <math>A</math> and for each maximal ideal <math>\mathfrak m</math> of <math>A</math> such that <math>\operatorname{length}_B (B/ \mathfrak{m} B)</math> is finite, the natural inclusion <math>A \to B</math> is a [[faithfully flat ring homomorphism]] if and only if the theorem of transition holds between <math>A \subset B</math>.<ref name=Matsumura />
